author: Amelia Hobson
title: 'Never seen anything like it' High winds cause damage and power outages throughout Utah - NewsBreak
text:
By Amelia Hobson McKenzie Diaz ,
5 hours ago
SALT LAKE CITY ( ABC4 ) — High winds in Utah caused significant damage and impacted thousands of residents throughout the state.
According to Rocky Mountain Power, approximately 8500 customers were without power throughout Utah, with clusters of outages throughout Salt Lake County. At the peak of issues, there were approximately 150 outages. Now, as of 9:00 p.m., there are 89 active outages, still impacting more than 3700 customers.
Officials are still investigating the cause of many of the outages, though there are high wind warnings throughout Utah, which may be contributing to the outages.
At 1700 S 2100 E, there is a downed power line, caused by a tree that fell from the high winds, indicating one of the causes of current power outages. Salt Lake City Police Department confirmed it is blocking two blocks.
Other downed power lines at 21000 N in Plymouth, Box Elder County are causing delays. According to Box Elder County, the road is closed and may remain closed for multiple days while crews work in the area. They added, “Please avoid the area, use an alternate route, and never approach or drive over downed power lines.
The Box Elder County outage is estimated to be lifted around 1:30 a.m. on May 14.
Utahns react to damage Residents say they have seen extensive damage from the wind gusts. Carolyn Wood, who lives near the fallen tree in Salt Lake City, said, “I was almost blown over, the winds were so intense. [There’s] a lot of debris, because the winds were so high.”
Wood was walking in the neighborhood and was on a walk when trees started to fall. She added, “Then, it was like a domino effect, and just took out all of the power all the way up to 2030 E.”
Jacon Letey also heard the trees fall, “Heard a big bang. You can hear tress falling and sparks of fire. We don’t have power so I can’t microwave food or use the fridge. So, tonight, I will Doordash.”
1000-acre Wild Horse Fire, other wildfires spread amid gusty winds in Utah Unfortunately, the damage stretches far beyond Wood and Letey’s neighborhood, drawing in many onlookers.
“I’ve never seen anything like that,” said Josie Messersmith, who was just trying to make food when her power went out. “We had plans to cook dinner together tonight, and no power, and my stove doesn’t work, because of that. My house smells weird because I think everything in the fridge is rotting.”
“Theres a lot of damage here- Big branch crushed one of our neighbors’ fences,” added Jake Sandkyle.
Others say the uncertainty is hard, especially as they try to fulfill their responsibilities. Vilote Loeffler stated, “I need Wi-Fi to do some schoolwork.”
Wood added, “You know, my heart goes out to everyone without power.”
As of right now, the estimated restoration time for the outages vary significantly, lasting throughout the night in many areas. ABC4.com has reached out to Rocky Mountain Power (RMP) for more information and we are waiting to hear back at this time.
If you are experiencing a power outage and are a RMP customer, you can see updates on their website . Additionally, you can report an outage by texting OUT to 759677.
What to do during a power outage The American Red Cross recommends doing the following when you’re hit by a power outage.
Monitor local alerts for updates Contact your support network and let them know what’s going on Keep food cold, and when in doubt, throw it out Prevent power overloads and fire hazards by unplugging appliances and electronics Take caution to prevent carbon monoxide poisoning if using gas appliances Decide if you need to stay or go — depending on your situation, staying at home may not be viable if you have medical devices or need hot/cold air Latest headlines: Copyright 2026 Nexstar Media, Inc.
